limitations: The product observation and diagnostic trials are different runs on shared storage; no fixed improvement ratio or hardware-fault diagnosis.
Zero-attack control deliberately retains flood_limited=false and whole attack-suite ok=false. Other checks pass.
Raw trial wrapper returned1 while changing diagnostic file ownership after successful data capture and monitor cleanup. Measurement exit_code=0; ownership was repaired separately.
The initial idle trial overlaps the first app preparation, and that app loses final HTTP metrics due to an idle verification connection. Both are excluded from performance comparisons.
Trace matches show SATA request issue-to-completion waits and journal blocking. SSD internal work, controller, driver, interrupt timing, and power policy are not distinguished.
Target thread identities come from100ms samples; very short-lived threads could be absent from the target subset. Trace overrun/drop counters are0.
Retained helper hashes refer to final scripts; initial and raw trials used earlier runner cleanup and canary metadata revisions. The hostmon binary is identical across trials.
The canary writes additional real fsync I/O at most2Hz, and tracing adds overhead; diagnosis is not a production performance guarantee.
Large writes from another process recur, but early occurrences do not produce the same latency window. No specific external service is assigned sole causality.
